CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What This Package Does

openalexAPI serves a local Parquet corpus of OpenAlex works as a web API that answers like the OpenAlex API, so the same classic URLs, OQL and OQO queries (with group_by, sort, paging) run against local data, and openalexPro’s download functions work against it unchanged (pro_query(endpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:8000")). A static web page is included. Works only; project-sized corpora, not the whole snapshot.

Exported: prepare_corpus(), serve_corpus(), oqo_to_sql().

Request flow

GET /works?filter=&search=&group_by=   --> POST {root}/query {oxurl}  (OpenAlex, free) --+
GET /?oql=  /  POST / {oql}            --> POST {root}/query {oql}                      --+--> OQO
GET /?oqo=  /  POST / {oqo}            ------------------------------------ (offline) ---+
POST /query                            --> forwarded to OpenAlex unchanged (openalexPro via = "oqo")
OQO --> oqo_to_sql() (registry) --> .api_execute() / .api_execute_groups() --> JSON built by DuckDB
File Role
R/corpus.R prepare_corpus(): cached DuckDB db per corpus state; works table + oaapi_* helper columns, FTS tables
R/registry_works.R filter registry (column_id -> SQL) and .api_groups_works() (group keys)
R/search.R search columns (<field>.search[.exact]): BM25, phrases, wildcards
R/oqo_to_sql.R tree walk: AND/OR/negation, NULL-safe leaves, sort, group spec, relevance score
R/execute.R records and grouped responses, paging, sample, single works
R/translate.R OpenAlex /query calls (httr2), cache
R/routes.R plumber2 app, serve_corpus(), the page (/app, /assets/)
inst/www/ page: index.html (template, {{v}} = asset stamp), query.js (pure, tested), app.js (DOM)
inst/extdata/oqo_translations.* recorded /query survey (see tools/)

Key design decisions (keep these)

  • Translation is OpenAlex’s, via its free POST /query; there is no local OQL/URL parser. Called with httr2 directly, not openalexPro::pro_translate(): the forwarded POST /query must return OpenAlex’s status and body unchanged. OpenAlex validation errors are passed through as they are (.api_abort(body = ...)).
  • Registry keys come from the survey, not the docs. tools/spike_translate.R records which OQO column_id OpenAlex emits for each classic filter (tools/spike_findings.md): e.g. search= -> fulltext.search, cites: -> referenced_works, title.search -> display_name.search, from_publication_date stays its own column, an equality leaf has no operator key, ranges are two leaves, null values mean “field missing”. Re-run it when OpenAlex changes; a new or renamed column_id is a 400 here until the registry has it.
  • Group key formats were surveyed live (all groupable columns): IDs as stored, slugs under https://openalex.org/<entity>/, plain years/counts/booleans/oa_status/institution types. Groups use an identity g (id_key() for IDs). :include_unknown is refused by OpenAlex’s translator, so GET /works strips it and passes it as a view flag.
  • Response JSON is built by DuckDB (to_json(struct_pack(...))) and pasted into the envelope; never round-trip records through jsonlite (empty arrays, nulls, int64, nesting). Group rows are small and go through .api_json(rows, na = "null").
  • / stays JSON-only for queries; without oql/oqo it redirects to /app. plumber2 picks the serializer by Accept, and httr2 (openalexPro) sends none, so HTML and JSON on one route would mislabel JSON and openalexPro would reject it.
  • IDs match in any form: id_key() / doi_key() SQL macros (R twins .api_id_key(), .api_doi_key()), applied to both sides; no assumption about the letter prefix (wZ… IDs).
  • The corpus: all *.parquet below the folder, works files only (id + title/ display_name), union_by_name, no hive columns, deduplicated on id_key(id). Extra columns are served as they are. Not served: .api_not_served (page, citation, abstract, relevance_score) and oaapi_*. abstract_inverted_index is rebuilt for JSONL-path corpora (round-trips exactly). Filter columns whose type differs between files are cast back (.api_column_types). The snapshot’s abstract_inverted_index is a JSON string: cast to MAP(VARCHAR, BIGINT[]) via JSON; records with repeated keys (~0.6 %) fail that cast and are merged by .api_merge_duplicate_keys() (json_each).
  • .api_build_version is part of the cache key: bump it whenever .api_build() (or anything it creates) changes, or users keep a stale cache.
  • Search: two FTS tables (oaapi_docs_stem Porter + English stop words, oaapi_docs_exact none), conjunctive BM25 (OpenAlex ANDs words, checked live), phrases and wildcards as regex on oaapi_title/oaapi_abstract; relevance_score = sum over non-negated search leaves.
  • Search terms are computed once per request (oqo_to_sql()$prelude, run by .api_run_prelude()): each BM25 query into a temp table oaapi_s<n>(i, s), the leaf is oaapi_id IN (SELECT i FROM oaapi_s<n>), the score one lookup in oaapi_score. Never put match_bm25() per work into the WHERE or ORDER BY: on 11,000 works a 20-term OR took 21 s that way (now 0.3 s) and OpenAlex’s 114-term example did not finish (now 1.7 s). Anything that runs an oqo_to_sql() result must run its prelude first.
  • Samples must be identical on every page: always seeded (from the query if none), input ordered by oaapi_id, SET threads = 1 for the query.
  • Grouped requests run the filter once into temp tables (oaapi_m, oaapi_g); fine on the read-only connection, requests are handled one at a time.
  • Errors: .api_abort(message, status, body); DuckDB binder errors (a struct field the corpus lacks) become a 400 in .api_get().

DuckDB notes

  • Connections via .api_con() (R/utils_duckdb.R), which loads json and fts explicitly: autoinstall_known_extensions is FALSE, so autoloading fails on fresh CI runners.
  • Lambdas use the new syntax lambda x: …; the arrow form x -> … is an error in duckdb 2.0.
  • SELECT * EXCLUDE (...) REPLACE (...): EXCLUDE comes first.

Speed

tools/benchmark.R downloads an ~11,000-work corpus once and times every feature (filters, paging, sample, every group_by, all search forms, the 114-term example); run it after changes to the compiler or execution. On 11,000 works everything is under 0.35 s except the 114-term search (1.7 s); building the database takes ~2 s. Scaling on snapshot partitions (10k to 9.6M works, tools/benchmark_scaling.csv, figure tools/plot_scaling.R -> man/figures/scaling.svg, shown in the README): queries stay flat while the database fits in RAM (~7 GB per million works) and slow down sharply beyond. The build must not keep whole rows in memory: the dedup window function runs only when ids repeat, preserve_insertion_order = false.

Docker

docker/ (Dockerfile, serve.R entrypoint with a prepare argument, compose.yaml with Caddy pulling the published image, compose.build.yaml to build from the checkout instead). The image installs the package from the checkout; the corpus is mounted at /corpus, the database lives in a /cache volume. Build from the package root: docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t openalexapi . (colima works). .github/workflows/docker.yaml publishes ghcr.io/openalexpro/openalexapi on each release (and manual runs: branch tag), amd64 and arm64 on native runners, merged by digest. The vignette points at main’s docker/compose.yaml and Caddyfile, so keep those working.

Common Commands

devtools::load_all()
devtools::document()
devtools::test()          # NOT_CRAN=true for the server tests
devtools::check(vignettes = FALSE)
serve_corpus("tests/testthat/fixtures/corpus_jq", port = 8790)   # try the page

devtools::build_readme() fails (it installs the package and cannot resolve openalexPro from CRAN); README chunks are not evaluated, so render with rmarkdown::render("README.Rmd") and delete README.html.

Tests

  • Fixtures (tools/make_fixtures.R): corpus_jq (369 works, JSONL shape: abstract, no inverted index; from openalexConvert) and corpus_api (2 works, API shape; from openalexPro). Variants with mixed ID forms, missing names or mixed types are built inside the tests.
  • test-server.R starts serve_corpus() in a callr process (local_server() in helper.R). Tests that need OpenAlex’s /query (classic URLs, OQL, openalexPro round trips) use skip_if_offline("api.openalex.org"); OQO tests run offline.
  • Counts are always checked against hand-written SQL on the same fixture.
  • openalexPro round trips (pro_fetch(pro_query(..., endpoint = local)), via = "url" and "oqo", multi-page, grouped, search) are the compatibility contract: keep them passing.
  • test-page.R runs inst/www/query.js with V8; keep page logic that can be pure in query.js.

Branching

  • claude/<description> branches from dev; merge into dev; main gets release commits only.
  • Public since 0.1.0 (alpha); archived on Zenodo, concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24514237 (cite that one). Not on the openalexPro r-universe (it is not in the r-universe registry; add it there only when it leaves alpha); installed from GitHub. Listed on the org landing page (openalexpro.github.io) and org profile (dot-github) as Alpha.
  • Stacked PRs, merge in order: #1 filters, #2 group_by, #3 search, #4 page, #5 docs, #6 performance, #7 more filters (lineage, funders, affiliation/author search, proximity, …).

Coverage and parity

  • tools/oql_coverage.R runs OpenAlex’s OQL example corpus (156 of 174 runnable works queries run; the rest need collections, semantic search, multi-dimension group_by, comparisons or nested in (...) queries). Run it after adding registry columns.
  • tools/live_parity.R compares counts and groups with OpenAlex on a downloaded corpus; filter and group checks must be equal, full-text searches differ (OpenAlex also searches full texts).
  • Affiliation and author-name searches (.api_list_search_entry()) are regex over the lists, not FTS: words may come from different strings, a phrase must be within one (OpenAlex’s rule for these fields). Proximity is .api_prox_re(): up to N words between terms.
